claim.quote: the first weeks of operation in the new underground laboratory of Rustrel-Pays d'Apt already provide a sensitivity to axially-coupled Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) competitive with leading experiments

name: First Dark Matter Limits from a Large-Mass, Low-Background Superheated Droplet Detector
notes: Date: first arXiv submission (v1, 28 Jan 2000); the abstract quoted is that of the latest arXiv version (v3, last revised 29 Sep 2000).

summary.plain: SIMPLE's first large droplet modules, tested in the new underground laboratory at Rustrel, gave early limits on spin-dependent WIMPs that were competitive with the leading experiments.
summary.technical: First SIMPLE modules of about 15 g active mass; the abstract gives no numerical limit and says the data sample was small and statistically limited.

title: First Dark Matter Limits from a Large-Mass, Low-Background Superheated Droplet Detector
why_it_matters: The abstract says the result confirms superheated droplet detectors as a convenient, low-cost alternative for WIMP detection.
